svg.text: AWS Data Pipeline Starter Kit — Before / After

g.title: Before: ad-hoc, manual, and unguarded — bad data can land and costs can drift.
Files land in storage with no checks, so bad data can flow downstream unnoticed.
A Glue job run by hand, with no schedule or repeatable trigger, so runs are easy to miss.
Tables live in scattered places with no shared catalog, so teams guess at schemas.
Queries run directly on raw tables with no tests, so wrong results are found late.
No quality checks before data is used, so dashboards can show bad numbers.
Changes are deployed by hand with no checks, so a bad change can break the pipeline.
No limits or lifecycle rules, so costs can grow unnoticed.
Dashboards read raw data directly, so any upstream change breaks them.

svg.text: How it happens, step by step — follow the numbered nodes in order; each step hands its problems to the next.

g.title: After: event-driven validation, a catalogued medallion pipeline, tested marts, and CI/CD with cost guardrails.
Landing zone where files arrive; only validated files move on, bad ones are quarantined.
An event-driven validator that checks each file on arrival and records every outcome.
Bad files are held apart instead of landing, so nothing bad reaches the gold layer.
PySpark job that transforms bronze to silver to gold, building a clean star schema.
One schema registry shared by Athena, dbt and BI tools, so everyone sees the same tables.
SQL models with tests and docs that build trusted business marts on Athena.
Query layer with workgroup limits, so analysts query gold tables safely and cheaply.
Metrics and alerts on every outcome, so failures are seen at once, not by users.
All infrastructure as code with PR checks and automated deploys, so changes are safe and repeatable.
